cards.title: Addressing Iranian Air Force Seniors
cards.body: Iranian military ranks are hierarchical. Address seniors with their full rank and title. Avoid using first names unless invited. Use 'Doctor' for those with academic titles.

cards.title: Indirect Refusal in Iran
cards.body: Iranians often refuse indirectly to maintain politeness. Initial refusals are common and may not be genuine. Pay attention to nonverbal cues and context.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Iran (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Iran
cards.body: Iranian culture values hierarchy and respect for elders. When addressing seniors, use formal titles like 'agha' (Mr.) or 'khanoom' (Mrs./Ms.) followed by their last name. Maintain eye contact to show sincerity, but avoid prolonged eye contact with unrelated women in public.

cards.title: Saving Face in Iran
cards.body: Iranians value tact and indirect communication to avoid causing offense. When criticizing or disagreeing, do so privately and gently. If you must refuse, initially decline politely before accepting if necessary. Avoid public confrontations or direct refusals.

cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Carry identification and base passes. Women may face additional scrutiny. Remain calm and polite. Avoid discussing sensitive topics.

cards.title: Respecting Religious Hierarchy
cards.body: Iranian society is deeply influenced by Islam. Shi'a Islam has a clear hierarchy. Address seniors with respect, using their titles and avoiding familiarity. Be mindful of religious practices and customs.
doThis: Use formal titles when addressing seniors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Iran (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Religious Differences
cards.body: Islam is central to daily life. Be aware of prayer times and fasting during Ramadan. Avoid scheduling important meetings during these times. Respect local customs and traditions.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Iran (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving Hierarchy
cards.body: Iranians value hierarchy. Present gifts to seniors first, using both hands. Gifts are usually opened later. Avoid expensive gifts to avoid embarrassment. Practical gifts like chocolates or flowers are common.
doThis: Address seniors with their title and last name

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Iran (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving Etiquette
cards.body: Refuse a gift once or twice before accepting to show humility. Gifts are usually brought to the home or office. Avoid giving gifts that are too personal or expensive. Practical gifts like chocolates or flowers are common.
doThis: Refuse a gift once or twice before accepting
Bring gifts to the home or office
avoidThis: Insist on accepting a gift immediately

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Meals
cards.body: Iranian meals often involve hierarchy. Seniors are served first and may initiate conversations. Show respect by addressing them formally and waiting for their lead.
